chunks: From him, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hisham ibn al-Hakam, who said:

I was selling the sabiri (a type of fabric) in the shadows, so Abu al-Hasan Musa (peace be upon him) passed by me and said, 'O Hisham, indeed selling in the shadows is deception (ghishsh), and deception is not permissible.'

key_terms.اَلسَّابِرِيَّ: Sabiri, a type of fine fabric or cloth
key_terms.غِشٌّ: Deception or fraud, specifically in trade
key_terms.فِي اَلظِّلاَلِ: In the shadows, referring to areas with insufficient light or obscurity

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on selling goods in the shadows in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam Musa al-Kadhim (AS) identifies selling in shadows as *ghishsh* (deception/concealment of defects), a concept central to Shia commercial jurisprudence regarding the validity of sales. This ruling underscores the ethical imperative of transparency, ensuring that buyers are not misled by environmental obscurity, thereby reinforcing the principle that trade must be conducted with clear knowledge of the goods' condition.
